# agent-wrapped

> A local-first CLI that reads your own Claude Code transcripts and renders a
> "wrapped" card of how you actually work — read:write token ratio, cache share,
> subagent share, tool mix, streaks and hourly rhythm. It makes no network calls,
> has zero runtime dependencies, and never prints your repository names.

Run it with `npx @lfgcampos/agent-wrapped` on Node 22 or newer. Nothing is uploaded, there is
no account, and there is no telemetry: it reads `~/.claude/projects` and
`~/.claude/settings.json` read-only and renders locally.

It also warns when Claude Code's transcript retention (`cleanupPeriodDays`, ~30 days
by default) is about to delete history you have not summarised yet, and saves a ~1 KB
snapshot per run so you can keep years of history without keeping years of transcripts.

## Docs

- [Full documentation, in Markdown](https://agent-wrapped.dev/index.md): the complete
  landing page — install, options, what each number divides by, and FAQ.
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lfgcampos/agent-wrapped/main/README.md):
  the same material as shipped on npm and GitHub.
- [CONTRIBUTING](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lfgcampos/agent-wrapped/main/CONTRIBUTING.md):
  the design rules that are deliberate — no network calls, no dependencies, no
  currency figures, no personality scoring.
- [CHANGELOG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lfgcampos/agent-wrapped/main/CHANGELOG.md):
  what changed in each version.

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/lfgcampos/agent-wrapped): about a thousand
  lines of TypeScript, MIT licensed, readable in one sitting.
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lfgcampos/agent-wrapped): published with npm
  trusted publishing (OIDC), so every release carries a provenance attestation.

## Optional

- [whatkindof.dev](https://whatkindof.dev): a developer personality test by the same
  author. It asks how you think you work; agent-wrapped reads what your logs say.
